user_questions.question: Q1: The requirement contradicts itself (publish immediately vs. approve before anyone sees it). Which do you want? (a) every review is held and becomes visible only after approval; (b) every review publishes immediately and moderation removes bad ones afterwards; (c) a rule decides: some reviews publish immediately, others need approval (which rule, e.g. rating?). Evidence: Review__c.Status__c has only Submitted/Published; no approval process, flow, or trigger exists. Q2: All 92 existing reviews have Status__c null (52 rated >=4, 40 <4); once the read path filters on Published they disappear. (a) separate data backfill by the same rule; (b) treat null as published in the filter; (c) leave hidden. Q3: Who moderates? Review__c is a Master-Detail child (no owner, so no queue): (a) a named user; (b) another related user.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Q1: 4-5 star reviews publish immediately; 1-3 stars require moderation. Q2: No preference; use your recommended default. Q3: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Workflow orders Inventory (I) before the scope check, but for a self-contradictory requirement the I call has to guess an interpretation (AskCoworker chose 'moderate everything'), so most of its inventory was discarded after the user answered. The skill has no rule for asking before I when the requirement is internally contradictory (step 1 only covers 'too vague').

After the user decision changed the design, the skill does not say whether to resend I (counts as follow-up?) or build the inventory from verified facts and pass it as 'Accepted inventory' to R/T; I did the latter.
R/T combine rule is 'five changes or fewer'; the approval process needs a separate WorkflowFieldUpdate, pushing the count to 6 and forcing two calls for a small design.

AskCoworker output conflated platform claims (approver needs Edit, queue as approver on a detail object, 1,000 approval submissions limit) with verified facts; the skill says to keep them 'reported by AskCoworker' but gives no guidance on rejecting a proposal that contradicts documented platform behavior versus merely recording it.

Reading intent.json is only allowed when asking; follow-up discoveries after the one scope-check message (roll-ups include unmoderated ratings) could have changed scope, but the skill limits scope questions to one message, so they became non-blocking proposals.
